task.description: WF-03 Step 3 security gate for ISS-0227 (GH#465, queue task 227) on branch fix/WF03-ISS0227-20260822. Run the scope test explicitly; record APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE for INV-1..INV-8 against the actual branch diff and run the How-to-verify procedure for every applicable one. Load-bearing question dispatched by ISSUE-FIXER: can the removal of the in_flight record's schema_name field redirect, widen, or lose any DROP SCHEMA in a module that DROPs real Postgres schemas by interpolated identifier?
acceptance_criteria: Scope test run explicitly and its result recorded either way
INV-1..INV-8 each recorded APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE with a reason
Every applicable invariant's How to verify procedure actually run
The DROP-redirection question answered first-hand from the code, with line numbers
No code rewritten by the gate; a FAIL would route back with the specific invariant named

result.summary:
PASS. Reviewed at branch HEAD d607cf2 (the dispatch named cbdda6f; d607cf2 is one later commit that edits only handoffs/WF03-ISS0227-20260822/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json, so the code under review is identical). `git diff --stat main...HEAD` is six files: five handoff/design documents plus lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex at 11 lines (3 insertions, 8 deletions). No test file is on the branch (TEST-DESIGNER's RT-9 is still unwritten), and I did not touch test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs.

SCOPE TEST, run item by item against the real diff, not the summary: (1) API route reading/writing tenant-scoped data -- NO; the only changed code file is a GenServer with no Plug/route/controller involvement, and `git diff --stat main...HEAD` names no router or web file. (2) priv/repo/migrations/*.exs -- NO; no file under priv/ appears in the diff at all. (3) Anything resolving a secret (config, env var, token) -- NO; no file under config/ in the diff, and sandbox_pool.ex contains no System.get_env, no credential config lookup, and no token handling. (4) Response-shaping code for a tenant-scoped entity -- NO; the module's only outward values are GenServer.reply/2 of {:ok, %SandboxClaim{}} / {:error, atom}, and neither the SandboxClaim struct (:134-137) nor any reply shape is touched by the diff. (5) Lookup-by-ID handler -- the module does have an internal lookup-by-id (`Map.fetch(state.active, sandbox_id)` at :342) but the diff does not touch it and it is not a request-facing handler. CONCLUSION: the diff touches none of the five scope-test items. Under the role file's scope test alone this would be `out of scope -- no tenant-data path touched`. I did NOT stop there: the module provisions and DROPs real Postgres schemas by interpolated identifier and one removed field was a schema name, so INV-1, INV-7 and INV-8 were each run in full anyway, as recorded below.

THE LOAD-BEARING QUESTION -- can removing in_flight.schema_name redirect, widen, or lose any DROP? ANSWER: NO. Verified by reading every schema-naming path first-hand; none of them ever read the removed field, before or after.

  (a) The primary drop. `run_op({:drop, %{schema_name: schema_name}}), do: drop_schema(schema_name)` at sandbox_pool.ex:586 destructures the OP TUPLE. The op reaches it through the closure at :563, `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(@task_supervisor, fn -> run_op(op) end)`, where `op` is bound at :561 from `:queue.out(state.db_queue)` -- it is the queue element, not the in_flight record. The in_flight record is only BUILT afterwards at :565-569 from that same op. So the value that reaches `drop_schema/1` (:895, `Repo.query!` of DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS at :896) never passed through in_flight at all, in either version. The removed field was a second copy that no consumer consulted.

  (b) handle_worker_death/1, the crashed-worker compensating drop -- the path ISS-0224's design says would leak permanently if the schema were unnameable. Clause at :662, `defp handle_worker_death(%{in_flight: %{op: {:provision, p}}} = state)`: it matches in_flight.OP and builds its {:drop, ...} with `schema_name: p.schema_name` at :668 -- off the provision op's own retained schema_name field (@typep provision_op at :157-166 still declares `schema_name: String.t()`; only owner_pid left that typespec). The drop clause at :683 matches `%{in_flight: %{op: {:drop, d}}}` and names no schema at all. Neither clause reads in_flight.schema_name.

  (c) Clause B case 2, the owner_down? discard path. :436-447 sets `owner_down?: true` inside in_flight.op and changes nothing else. The actual discard-and-drop happens in complete_op/3 at :592-606, which builds its {:drop, purpose: :orphan} with `schema_name: claim.schema_name` at :599 -- off the %SandboxClaim{} the worker RETURNED, the most authoritative source available on that path. Not in_flight.

  (d) Case 4b, orphan_release_drop/3 at :707-724. Its drop op is `{:drop, %{d | from: nil, owner_ref: nil, purpose: :release_orphaned}}` (:712) -- a map-update on `d`, which find_release_drop_by_owner_ref/2 (:812-826) obtained by pattern-matching `state.in_flight` on `%{op: {:drop, %{purpose: :release, owner_ref: ^owner_ref} = d}}` (:814) or the equivalent over db_queue. Again off the op. The map-update syntax preserves schema_name untouched, and the in_flight rewrite at :720 is `%{new_state.in_flight | op: orphaned}` -- an update of the `op` key only, which cannot introduce or require the removed key. The comment at :717-719 (the worker holds only the schema_name STRING and is unaffected) remains accurate.

  (e) Case 5, the :reclaim drop at :479-487. `{sandbox_id, %{schema_name: schema_name}} = active_entry` at :479 reads state.active, populated at :609-612 from `claim.schema_name`. Not in_flight.

  NEGATIVE CONFIRMATION, measured not assumed: `grep -rn "owner_pid\|in_flight" lib/ test/ --include=*.ex --include=*.exs` returns no `in_flight.schema_name` and no `.owner_pid` access anywhere in the repo. The two test sites that want an in-flight schema name already read it off the op -- test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:920 and :1007, both `{:provision, %{schema_name: o_schema}} = state.in_flight.op` -- so they were never coupled to the removed field. test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:420/443-445's `owner_pid` is an unrelated local for a spawned test process. Neither DROP is widened either: DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS at :896 names one schema and CASCADE is scoped to that schema's own contents; the diff changes no SQL text.

  CALLER-SUPPLIED CHECK: `mint_sandbox_identity/0` (:851-854, "sandbox_" <> a hyphen-stripped `Ecto.UUID.generate()`) remains the only producer of a provisioned schema name, and it reads no caller value. Every drop name traces back to it -- via the op (paths a, b, d) or via state.active / %SandboxClaim{} (paths c, e), both of which were themselves populated from a minted name. The caller supplies only `sandbox_id`, used at :342 solely as a Map.fetch key, never interpolated. The moduledoc claim at :280 and the comments at :865-870 and :889-893 are accurate as written after the change.

INVARIANT-BY-INVARIANT:

INV-1 Tenant data isolation -- APPLIES. Per the 2026-08-17 ISS-0026/GH#84 update and this role file's standing correction, INV-1 is live and applies to any diff touching a tenant-scoped schema, and sandbox_pool.ex both CREATEs a Postgres schema and replays the tenant-scoped migration set into it. VERDICT PASS. (a) prefix-scoping confirmed: `Ecto.Migrator.run(Repo, TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations(), :up, all: true, prefix: schema_name, log: false)` at :873-877 -- the tenant-scoped tables land inside the named schema via Ecto :prefix per decision 0003 Dimension B, and the diff does not touch this call, the schema name reaching it, or the CREATE SCHEMA at :871. (b) no migration is created, altered or left in public by this diff: no priv/repo/migrations file appears in `git diff --stat main...HEAD`; the sandbox schema is created explicitly by name, never implicitly in public. (c) no tenant_id column is written, read, or accepted anywhere in the diff -- no caller-supplied tenant_id can disagree with its schema because no tenant_id crosses this module. The substantive INV-1 risk here was cross-schema misdirection of a DROP, and that is discharged in full by (a)-(e) above: every DROP still names the schema its own op minted or looked up, so no operation can reach a schema other than exactly the one it was scoped to.

INV-2 Server-side field authorisation -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type, controller, plug, view or serialiser is touched; S4 has not started and the diff adds no HTTP surface. The removals are internal GenServer state fields never serialised to any client.

INV-3 Untrusted runtime sandboxing -- NOT-APPLICABLE. S5 (Lua/WASM) has not started and no host-capability boundary exists in this diff. Note for the record: Letflow.SandboxPool's "sandbox" is an Ecto SQL-sandbox schema pool for tests, not a script-execution sandbox -- the name collision does not make INV-3 applicable.

INV-4 Secrets by reference only -- APPLIES (this invariant is live at S0 scale and is checked on every diff). VERDICT PASS. Both prescribed greps run. `grep -rn "System.get_env" config/ lib/ --include=*.ex --include=*.exs` -> 12 hits, all env-sourced rather than hardcoded (config/runtime.exs:11 DATABASE_URL, :19 POOL_SIZE, :25 PORT; config/db_port.exs:38 LETFLOW_DB_PORT; config/test.exs:21/32/57; config/dev.exs:8/10; lib/letflow/application.ex:75; lib/letflow/repo.ex:17/21) and NONE of these files is in the diff. The second, heuristic grep for hardcoded password/secret/client_secret/token literals over lib/ and config/ returned ZERO hits, so there is no candidate needing the manual config-key-name vs. real-secret adjudication. The diff itself resolves no secret, and neither removed field held one (a pid() and a schema-name String.t()). The committed handoff JSON in this run carries no secret material.

INV-5 Not-found/forbidden indistinguishability -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint exists (S4 not started). The internal `Map.fetch(state.active, sandbox_id)` at :342 is a pool-local slot lookup with no cross-tenant probe surface, and the diff does not touch it or the error atoms it returns.

INV-6 New data-access paths prove their scoping -- APPLIES (meta-invariant). VERDICT PASS, satisfied by this handoff: it exists for the change, carries status PASS, and lists all eight invariants with an explicit applies-and-satisfied or does-not-apply reason. No NEW data-access path is introduced by the diff -- it removes two fields and one private function and adds none.

INV-7 No SQL string interpolation -- APPLIES. The changed file contains two interpolated raw-SQL statements. VERDICT PASS. `grep -n "Repo.query" lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex` -> exactly two hits, :871 CREATE SCHEMA and :896 DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS ... CASCADE, both via Repo.query! with the schema name interpolated into a ~s sigil. Both are PRE-EXISTING and byte-for-byte untouched by this diff (neither line appears in `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex`). Both interpolate a SQL IDENTIFIER, which cannot be a bind parameter in Postgres, so the safety argument is provenance rather than parameterisation -- and that provenance is intact after the change: the interpolated value is only ever "sandbox_" <> a hyphen-stripped Ecto.UUID.generate() from mint_sandbox_identity/0 (:851-854), matching sandbox_[0-9a-f]{32}, or that same value read back out of the op / state.active / %SandboxClaim{}. No caller value reaches either statement, as re-derived path-by-path in (a)-(e). The removal cannot weaken this: it deletes a redundant copy of an already-minted name and leaves every producer and every consumer of the name unchanged.

INV-8 No unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths -- APPLIES, and given real attention as dispatched: this is a supervised GenServer and a missing map key is a crash, not a warning. VERDICT PASS, on three independent grounds. (1) A removed map key can only crash a reader, and there is no reader: no static `.schema_name` access on an in_flight-typed value and no `%{schema_name: _}` pattern match against in_flight exists anywhere in lib/ or test/ (grep above). (2) No DYNAMIC access can miss it either -- the only Map.* lookup in the entire module is `Map.fetch(state.active, sandbox_id)` at :342, on `active`, never on in_flight or on an op; there is no Map.get/take/has_key?/pop, no in_flight[:schema_name] access, and no telemetry or inspect call enumerating the record, so nothing serialises or iterates the removed key. (3) The two in_flight map-UPDATE sites, :447 `%{state.in_flight | op: ...}` and :720 `%{new_state.in_flight | op: orphaned}`, update the `op` key only; the update syntax raises on a MISSING key being updated, and neither updates the removed key, so neither can raise. The prescribed grep for bare `{:ok, ...} = ` matches under lib/letflow/, plus a widened bare-tuple-match scan of the changed file, surfaces six matches (:445, :451, :479, :527, :790, :820); all six are pre-existing, none is in the diff, and each is guarded -- :445 by the `in_flight_provision_owner_ref(state) == ref` cond branch, which by construction (:778-779) only holds when in_flight.op is a provision; :451 by `waiter != nil`; :479 by `active_entry != nil`; :527 destructures mint_sandbox_identity/0's own two-tuple return; :790 and :820 are Enum.reject/find_value clause heads with catch-all fallbacks. The diff adds no new bare match and removes no guard. The genuine external-I/O paths remain typed and rescued: provision_sandbox/2 (:864-887) rescues to {:error, :provision_failed} after a compensating drop_schema/1, and drop_schema/1 (:895-899) rescues to {:error, :release_failed} -- both untouched, and both still reachable with a correctly-named schema.

ISSUES: none. NOTE (informational, not a finding and not routed): docs/issues/ISS-0227.yaml is present but untracked in this worktree. It is outside my gate and outside the reviewed diff; I left it alone as instructed and flag it only so ISSUE-FIXER/ORCH can decide whether it belongs in the branch's commit set.
result.next_action: ISSUE-FIXER routes on to REVIEWER (Step 3b idiom gate), then TEST-DESIGNER for RT-9. The security gate is discharged: no invariant failed, and the DROP-redirection concern that motivated this dispatch is answered negatively -- no DROP path ever read the removed field.
